concurrent_post.true_db_level_race_vs_serialization_disc: Both requests returned a clean redirect to the identical child with exactly one queued dispatch, which is the REQUIRED observable outcome either way. Whether MySQL's row lock was genuinely contended (one transaction blocking on FOR UPDATE while the other held it, then resolving via the QueryException/isRecoveryLineageUniqueViolation catch path) or the two requests were serialized earlier by PHP-FPM/OS scheduling such that the second transaction did not begin until after the first had already committed (resolving via the ordinary existingChild pre-check) could not be conclusively distinguished from outside the database engine in this environment -- no lock-wait/transaction-timing instrumentation was captured. This is reported as an open question, not claimed as a confirmed true-race observation, per instruction.
